verifications.llm_reasoning: WP_EGFEGFR_SIGNALING is a generic EGF/EGFR signaling pathway and does not capture the key disease-specific biology in the original name and rationale: activating EGFR mutations in cancer with constitutive signaling and TKI sensitivity/resistance context. A Reactome cancer-variant pathway is a better semantic and biological match, and Reactome has higher priority than WikiPathways. Among the candidates, Constitutive Signaling by Ligand-Responsive EGFR Cancer Variants best reflects activating EGFR mutations in NSCLC.

The original pathway describes the RAS–RAF–MEK–ERK (MAPK) cascade itself, especially its activation in KRAS/BRAF-driven resistance. WP_EGFR_TYROSINE_KINASE_INHIBITOR_RESISTANCE is broader and focuses on drug resistance rather than the MAPK cascade mechanism. Among the candidates, REACTOME_ONCOGENIC_MAPK_SIGNALING is a closer biological match and has higher priority than WikiPathways.

The current WikiPathways mapping is too broad and describes metastatic trait amplification rather than the specific MET/HGF signaling axis. The biology in the prompt is explicitly MET/HGF-driven bypass signaling in EGFR-TKI resistance, which is directly captured by the higher-priority Reactome pathway 'Signaling by MET'. This is a much closer and more precise match than the current mapping.

REACTOME_EGFR_DOWNREGULATION is not a good match because the original pathway describes EGFR-driven oncogenic signaling leading to VEGF/angiogenesis and PD-L1-mediated immune evasion, not receptor downregulation. Among the candidates, REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_EGFR_IN_CANCER best captures the core EGFR oncogenic biology and is more appropriate than a downregulation term. HALLMARK_ANGIOGENESIS reflects only one downstream component and does not cover the EGFR/PD-L1 context as well.

The current mapping to a generic apoptosis term is not the best fit. The original pathway describes the ELK1–CIP2A–AKT survival axis downstream of ERK, with afatinib acting through EGFR/ERBB inhibition to suppress this pro-survival signaling and induce apoptosis. This is primarily an EGFR/ERBB cancer signaling pathway rather than a standalone apoptosis pathway. Among the candidates, REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_EGFR_IN_CANCER captures the upstream biology most directly and is higher priority than the current WikiPathways apoptosis mapping.
